title: Orchard and Summer
premise: Sebastian 'Seb' Winterbourne, granddaughter of a lighthouse keeper and a part-time novelist, has spent ten years keeping her heart in careful training — until a snowstorm strands her at Hollow Orchard Vineyard with Theo Marsh, the rival she loved and lost in their twenties, and his business partner, the woman he nearly married. Trapped through winter in the vineyard's found family of misfit workers, Seb must confront the sentence she rehearsed for a decade: why she left, and that she never stopped loving him. As the first harvest approaches, she finally says it aloud, choosing belonging over safety, and the novel ends with the three rivals-turned-family pressing the season's first cider together as Theo and Seb begin again.
about_author: Juniper Dunmore is the pen name of a former orchard hand who wrote her first novel in a cider shed during a rain-soaked harvest season. She lives on the coast with an opinionated dog and a stubborn grapevine that refuses to die.

chapters.title: The Muscle That Lies
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. On the lighthouse gallery, Seb drafts the acknowledgments page of her debut novel and lies to herself about being content alone. Her editor calls: her book tour's final stop is Hollow Orchard Vineyard. Emotional beat: restless denial, the heart presented as a trained muscle.

chapters.title: Snow on the Coast Road
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The early storm hits as Seb drives to the vineyard; she skids into a ditch and is hauled out by a stranger who turns out to be Theo Marsh, her rival from culinary school and the man she abandoned ten years ago. Beat: shock, old wounds cracking open under new snow.

chapters.title: Two Rivals, One Roof
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Stranded by closed roads, Theo brings Seb to the farmhouse where his business partner, Imogen Hale, waits — the woman Theo almost married. The three circle each other like weather fronts. Beat: tense comedy of forced proximity and unfinished history.

chapters.title: What Imogen Knows
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Imogen recognizes Seb instantly from Theo's old stories and quietly decides not to say so. She observes the charged silence between them while running the household with brisk kindness. Beat: the reader learns Imogen is no villain, only tired of being a stand-in.

chapters.title: Pruning Season
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Roads stay buried; Seb stays to help prune vines for room and board. Theo teaches her the shears; their hands remember each other. A near-confession dies when Imogen calls them to dinner. Beat: warmth rekindling against Seb's will.

chapters.title: The Rehearsed Sentence
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, flashback-heavy. Ten years ago, Seb left Theo the night before his father's funeral, fleeing his grief and her own fear of being needed. We hear the sentence she has rehearsed ever since — 'I left because I was afraid you'd need me more than love me.' Beat: guilt given shape.

chapters.title: Cider House Rules
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The vineyard's ragtag crew — aging foreman Gus, runaway chef Priya, silent teen farmhand Cole — adopt Seb without ceremony, drafting her into cider nights and card games. Theo watches her belong and resents how easily it happens now. Beat: found family forming around the wound.

chapters.title: Imogen's Ledger
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. The vineyard is quietly failing; Imogen hides the ledger and considers selling to a resort developer. She needs Theo focused, not unraveling over Seb. Beat: stakes raised, sympathy complicated — Imogen begins lying to protect what she built.

chapters.title: Thaw, Briefly
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. A false spring opens the roads; Seb could leave and doesn't. She and Theo walk the frozen rows at night and almost kiss before Priya interrupts. Seb writes instead of speaking, burning the pages. Beat: desire outrunning discipline.

chapters.title: The Manuscript in the Drawer
chapters.summary: Cole's POV. Teenaged Cole, snooping for charger cables, finds Seb's unpublished manuscript — a thinly veiled novel about leaving a grieving man — and reads it in one night. He tells Imogen nothing but starts leaving anonymous notes quoting it. Beat: secrets migrating between characters.

chapters.title: Frost Warning
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. A late frost threatens the budding vines; the whole crew fights it all night with smudge pots and candles. In the exhausted dawn, Theo and Seb fall into each other — truly this time — then wake to Imogen watching from the porch. Beat: passion and its immediate cost.

chapters.title: What Imogen Says
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Imogen confronts Seb privately, not with fury but with the ledger: if the sale goes through, everyone keeps a home; if Theo wavers, everything falls. She asks Seb to leave after bud break. Beat: antagonist-by-circumstance makes her most human plea.

chapters.title: Departure, Delayed
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. Seb packs, writes Theo a letter explaining everything except the sentence, and leaves it unsigned in his truck. At the coast road, her car fails again — the same ditch, the same irony. Beat: fate refusing to let her rehearse her way out.

chapters.title: The Letter He Reads Twice
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo finds the letter, reads it twice, and understands at last why she left — but not whether she stayed because of him or the snow. He says nothing, tucks it away, and works beside her in brutal silence. Beat: misunderstanding sharpened by restraint.

chapters.title: Harvest Hands
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs braided. Harvest begins; every hand is needed. Seb, Theo, and Imogen work rows apart, communicating through Gus's shouted orders. Cole's anonymous notes escalate, quoting Seb's manuscript back at her on folded paper. Beat: communal momentum, private dread.

chapters.title: The Developer's Offer
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. The resort developer arrives in person, charming and patient, and Imogen signs a letter of intent — then finds Theo's grandfather's deed restriction in the archive, which voids any sale without family consent. Beat: hope and betrayal entangled; Imogen must confess her secrecy.

chapters.title: Everything Said Except It
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. The crew confronts Imogen; Theo learns of the letter of intent and the hidden ledger in one blow. Amid the fallout, Theo demands the truth from Seb about the past. She gives him everything — history, fear, apology — except the rehearsed sentence. Beat: climax deferred by one word too few.

chapters.title: Pressing Day
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. First press day: the whole harvest crushed in a single morning. Theo, hollowed out, almost signs the developer's papers himself — until Cole hands him the manuscript pages and the unsigned letter together, and he finally sees the sentence she couldn't say. Beat: revelation through other people's courage.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Spoken
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV. At dusk in the empty press house, Seb finds Theo waiting among the barrels. No rehearsal survives contact; she says the sentence badly, crying, true: she left because needing him terrified her, and she has loved him for ten years anyway. Beat: the emotional climax — vulnerability chosen over control.

chapters.title: Imogen's Choice
chapters.summary: Imogen's POV. Imogen tears up the letter of intent, tells the developer the orchard isn't for sale, and asks — not begs — to stay on as partner. Theo agrees; Seb offers friendship honestly. Beat: the rival becomes family; the love triangle dissolves into a trio.

chapters.title: First Cider
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The crew presses the season's first cider on the farmhouse porch — Gus toasting, Priya cooking, Cole reading Seb's dedication aloud from her finished acknowledgments page, which names them all. Beat: belonging made ritual, joy earned collectively.

chapters.title: Orchard and Summer
chapters.summary: Sebastian's POV, epilogue. One year later: the lighthouse lamp lit, the vines heavy, Seb's second novel dedicated to 'the people who taught my heart it wasn't a muscle after all.' Theo proposes clumsily among the rows; Imogen witnesses. Beat: resolution — identity, love, and home reconciled.
